Cool! This has fixed the first set of issues that I mentioned earlier with custom elements.

Now I'm only seeing the second case I've mentioned above but misdiagnosed root cause of. I think I also understand that second issue much better now. The issue there also seems caused by adoption happening earlier now, specifically here: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt, along the same lines.

Seen for these WPTs regressing:
- [importNode should clone a template content using the global registry by default](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/72b780fda14c724024341740bb7ce5672d8ee794/custom-elements/registries/Document-importNode.html#L102)
- [importNode should clone a template content using a specified scoped registry](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/72b780fda14c724024341740bb7ce5672d8ee794/custom-elements/registries/Document-importNode.html#L113)
- [importNode should clone a template content with a nested template element using a scoped registry](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/72b780fda14c724024341740bb7ce5672d8ee794/custom-elements/registries/Document-importNode.html#L136)

NB: For all of above the issue is actually before the clone happens.


Problem is that:

- During fragment parsing for `template.innerHTML`, the parser first creates and inserts the wrapper `<div>`
- That insertion adopts the `<div>`, and [document adoption](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt) rewrites its null custom element registry to the adopting document’s effective global registry
- Since parser element creation derives the registry from "intended parent", it sees the `<div>`’s rewritten global registry instead of the template contents’ intended null registry
- This allows descendants of the `<div>` to upgrade during template.innerHTML

Perhaps this needs special casing for template document and the registry? From what I gather, we need to hook this case into step 6 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token
